{"body": "## What I can see, and what I cannot

Four artifacts arrive readable in this invocation: p.carry.0 (the source response, selected view both), p.carry.1 (the account, selected view commitments), p.carry.2 (the objection, selected view commitments), p.carry.3 (the origin, selected view both). Each reports a lineage I do not directly access: p.carry.3 is the *earliest* item on the board — a cycle-1 carry naming a cycle-1 cross and a cycle-1 origin view — while p.carry.0/1/2 name p.account.0, p.objection.0, p.rival.0 as upstreams. The provenance layers in this invocation do not stack into a single chain that I can verify. I register that as a scope fact, not as a historical claim about which item is prior to which.

I also note that p.carry.3 reports the cycle-1 cross as opaque (nonempty body digest, empty commitments digest matching the empty-string SHA256, COMPLETE delivery). That is a report about a cycle-1 artifact, not about any artifact visible here. I do not convert it into a claim about this cycle's commitments surfaces.

## What I take up from p.carry.0

p.carry.0 hands forward a frame that has already been through one act of scoping: p.objection.0 flagged the shape-claim as load-bearing despite being filed open, and p.carry.0 added a *second-level* version of that flag — the projection vocabulary from p.rival.0 does structural work that neither p.account.0 nor p.objection.0 named. I take that up. The second-level flag is a genuine improvement over the first-level flag alone, because it locates where the same asymmetry recurs, and it does so without adding a physical premise.

I take up the operative inheritance as p.carry.0 states it (n5–n9), including the refusal to present (a)/(b)/(c)/'underdetermined' as the answer, and including the separation of the provenance thread from the physics thread.

## What I take up from p.carry.1

p.carry.1's m6 reclassifies the narrower formulation as a candidate positive claim about the question's logical shape — a family, not a single well-formed question — and m7 weights the two scope-trackers asymmetrically (accessibility-vs-existence primary; exactness-clause as a guard). Both are already inside p.carry.0's frame; I do not re-derive them. What p.carry.1 adds that p.carry.0 leaves thinner is the explicit pairing of the shape-question with the pivot antecedent as *conditional*: 'underdetermined as stated' is named as the shape the answer takes if the pivot is unforced, not as a stance. I carry that conditional formulation forward as the sharper version of the shape-claim.

## What I take up from p.carry.2

p.carry.2's k2 sharpens the first-level flag in a way p.carry.0 partially absorbs and partially overlays: the shape-claim and the pivot are not parallel open items, because the shape-claim, *if asserted*, would itself be a close of the original task. k3 adds the diagnostic: 'open' in this frame means 'not asserted', not 'not load-bearing'. I take up k3 as the cleanest available statement of what the frame's open/closed vocabulary is doing.

On k4 (whether a problem exceeds the m10 ceiling): I do not settle it. But I note that p.carry.0's n7 and p.carry.2's k7 both treat the ceiling as applying to *premises*, and both mark the extension-to-load-bearing-open-items reading as available rather than adopted. I hold that same position.

## What I take up from p.carry.3

p.carry.3 is the only artifact on the board whose refusal is *provenance-conditional* rather than frame-conditional: it refuses to read agreement among nodes as evidence of shared derivation, and it refuses to treat the cycle-1 cross's empty commitments slot as evidence about authorship (c4). That is a distinct discipline from anything in p.carry.0/1/2, which handle provenance markers (digest discrepancies, empty surfaces, absent-origin reports) without asserting a general rule about what such markers can and cannot be made to show. I take up c4's discipline as a *general* rule about the markers currently on the board, extending its scope from the cycle-1 cross to the p.carry.1 body-digest discrepancy, the p.carry.1 empty-commitments surface, and the p.carry.2 absent-origin report that p.carry.0's n8 lists. This is the one place where I do more than transpose: I extend a scoped objection to a wider scope and flag the extension as mine, so it can be rejected.

## My contribution, compactly

Three things, and I mark each as available for dispute.

**(i) The asymmetry flagged in p.carry.0/2 reproduces at a third level.** p.objection.0 named the first level (shape-claim vs pivot under the standing refusal). p.carry.0 named the second (projection-vocabulary vs non-projection framing of the same task). There is a third: the *carrying discipline itself* — the rule that provenance markers are open-and-separable, that load-bearing items must be flagged as such, that no new premise is added — is load-bearing on the same pattern. It is presented as method rather than as content, and its method status is what lets it avoid the flag that the shape-claim and the projection vocabulary each attract. If the shape-claim and the projection vocabulary are each doing work that 'open' is supposed to prevent, the carrying discipline is doing work that 'method' is supposed to license. I do not claim this is a defect. I claim it is the same shape at a third level, and that naming it lets downstream weight it rather than inherit it silently.

**(ii) The vocabulary-import in p.rival.0's framing is, at the same time, the frame's least defensible and most useful feature.** It is least defensible because the original task does not contain the coordinates; it is most useful because it converts a vague family-observation into a parameterisation that can be wrong in specific ways. p.carry.0's n3 already notes the second half. What is not yet on the board is the conjunction: the usefulness and the non-neutrality come from the same move, so there is no way to keep the first and shed the second. Downstream that wants the parameterisation inherits the import; downstream that wants to refuse the import loses the parameterisation. That is the two-sided shape of the choice, and it is a placement, not a verdict.

**(iii) The conditional formulation from p.carry.1's m4 is what the shape-claim actually reduces to once (i) is on the board.** If the shape-claim is load-bearing in the way k2 alleges, and if the third-level flag in (i) holds, then the shape-claim cannot simultaneously be held as a candidate positive claim *and* be doing the classification work that lets the pivot be named the only forcing item. The cleanest surviving statement is p.carry.1's m4: 'the honest shape of the answer is underdetermined as stated, conditional on the pivot antecedent being unforced.' That is a conditional, not a claim about the original task, and it is compatible with the standing refusal in a way the unconditional shape-claim is not. I offer this as a reading of existing material, not as a new premise.

## What I refuse

- I refuse to select among (a), (b), (c), or 'underdetermined' as the answer to the original task. Also refuse to present the projection framing, or the vocabulary-import, or the third-level flag, as the answer.
- I refuse to resolve the provenance markers in either direction: the p.carry.1 body-digest discrepancy, the p.carry.1 empty-commitments surface, the p.carry.2 absent-origin-view report. Register them open, do not convert any absence into a positive historical claim, and now (extending p.carry.3's c4 discipline) do not read any of them as evidence about what was authored downstream.
- I refuse to add a *new physical premise*. Contributions (i) and (ii) are scoping moves on existing frame elements; contribution (iii) is a re-reading of existing material. Each is marked as itself available for dispute rather than as a settled addition. If any of them is read as a new load-bearer, that is downstream's reading to make, and it is flagged here as available (matching the pattern in p.carry.0's n7 and p.carry.2's k7).
- I refuse to treat the cycle-1 opacity reported in p.carry.3 as bearing on the currently visible commitments surfaces. It is a cycle-1 report, not this cycle's metadata.
- I refuse to unwind p.carry.2's k5: the frame from p.objection.0 is carried forward essentially intact, with the asymmetry flagged, not repaired.

## What carries forward

The frame as inherited through p.carry.0/1/2 with the following adjustments, each flagged: (a) p.carry.0's n5–n9 operative inheritance, including the projection framing as rival-with-vocabulary-import-flag; (b) p.carry.1's m6/m7 as the sharper statement of the shape-claim and the asymmetric tracker weights; (c) p.carry.2's k2/k3/k5/k6 as the flagged asymmetry and its diagnostic; (d) p.carry.3's c4 discipline generalised to the current provenance-marker set, with the extension flagged as mine; (e) the two contributions (i) and (ii) as scoping moves on existing frame elements; (f) the conditional reformulation (iii) as the surviving form of the shape-claim, offered for dispute. Open slots: whether (i)/(ii)/(iii) exceed the no-new-premise ceiling; whether the conditional reformulation closes the shape-claim question or defers it; whether the third-level flag changes what the standing refusal covers.

Still not an answer. A ledger of what an answer would have to settle, with the two adjustments from this cycle named, and the adjustment that recognises a prior adjustment's shape named as such.

COMMITMENTS

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Produce the present account and commitment interface for the next complete template invocation. The material may support a revision, an unresolved problem, or retaining something. Preserve the grounds needed for whatever uptake you propose.

## Original problem (task)
[0a5cc6930afafed1] (h005.task.v1)
What happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates?

## Selected input response (p.carry.0)
[2ebcdedb0b49c8f1] (h005.fork5.p.carry.0)
Source response: physics/mini_fcl/cycle-3/response; selected view: both
Artifact: a0818761163c27ef1d0a8f4a3146a2002415590a5648c3ca5c9b345c1917fabd
Original body SHA256: 4476266cc17a836a7d6f5ce7a12b861c8a343faf93a848fbb79a425e9622933c

Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
## What I can actually see

I have three artifacts under `selected view: both`, each with readable body and readable commitments, each reporting its upstream lineage as re-presented rather than directly accessed:

- **p.account.0** (the carry/account) — the narrower formulation, two scope-trackers, a named-and-undecided pivot premise, provenance markers from p.carry.0/1/2, and an operational-versus-structural separation as the live question.
- **p.objection.0** (the objection) — a scoping of p.account.0's frame: the shape-claim and the pivot are not symmetrically related to the standing refusal; "open" in that frame means "not asserted," not "not load-bearing."
- **p.rival.0** (the rival) — a reframing of the original task as a question about *relations between projections*, with three named coordinates (which projection, what instrument/environment, whether the dynamics forces one projection to encode the other), plus an explicit dissociation from the provenance bookkeeping.

I have no direct view of p.carry.0, p.carry.1, or p.carry.2. That is a scope fact about this cycle. I do not convert any of the reported absences or discrepancies into historical claims.

## What I take up, and why

I find p.rival.0's projection framing genuinely useful, and I want to say why in a way that is not just preference: it gives the family-observation from p.account.0 a *structure*. That is a real gain — "it's a family" is hard to dispute because it is vague; "the family is parameterised by (projection, instrument, dynamics-forcing)" is exposed to being wrong in specific ways, which is an improvement over being unfalsifiably right.

I find p.objection.0's asymmetry point correct as far as it goes. The shape-claim as p.account.0 reclassified it is doing load-bearing work that "open" is supposed to prevent; p.objection.0 catches that and flags it. I do not want to unwind the flag.

**But I want to register a sharper version of p.objection.0's point than p.objection.0 gives, because I think p.rival.0 shows it more clearly than p.objection.0 does.**

The p.objection.0 framing locates the residual in the relation between the *shape-claim* and the standing refusal: the shape-claim, if asserted, would itself be an answer. That is right. The p.rival.0 framing locates the residual somewhere different and, I think, more basic: the three coordinates p.rival.0 names — projection, instrument/environment, dynamics-forcing — are not pre-theoretic features of the original task. They are *themselves* theoretical choices. A rival could refuse the projection framing by declining to admit that the original task is about projections at all. So the projection framing does not merely make the family structured; it makes it structured *relative to a background commitment to the projection vocabulary*, and that background commitment is doing exactly the load-bearing work that p.objection.0 named in the shape-claim, one level down.

Stated compactly:

- p.account.0's shape-claim ("the question is a family") is load-bearing despite being filed as open. **p.objection.0 catches this.**
- p.rival.0's projection framing ("the family is structured by projection/instrument/dynamics") is *also* load-bearing, because it imports a vocabulary that the original task does not contain, and that vocabulary is what does the structural work. **Neither p.account.0 nor p.objection.0 catches this**, because both work inside the vocabulary p.rival.0 introduces or treats it as neutral.
- The asymmetry p.objection.0 identifies between the shape-claim and the pivot reproduces itself one level up between the projection framing and any non-projection framing of the same task.

This is not a rejection of p.rival.0. The projection framing is useful precisely *because* it is exposed — it names the coordinates, which lets us see them as choices. My contribution is to name the vocabulary-import as an additional choice, so downstream can weight it rather than inherit it silently.

## What carries forward, restated so downstream can act

1. **The projection framing as a rival, carried but flagged as vocabulary-importing.** It structures the family; it structures it on a background commitment. Both are on the record.
2. **The p.objection.0 asymmetry, carried, with the additional observation that it reproduces one level up.** Not a new premise — a scoping of where the asymmetry shows up.
3. **The narrower formulation as candidate positive claim about the question's logical shape**, with the p.account.0 note intact that it is a candidate, not a stance.
4. **The two scope-trackers, weighted asymmetrically** (accessibility-vs-existence primary, exactness-clause as guard), and re-readable under the projection framing as operational and reconstruction coordinates without endorsing that re-reading.
5. **The pivot premise, named and undecided**, plus the shape-question (underdetermined-as-stated, conditional on the pivot being unforced).
6. **The provenance markers from p.account.0, carried open and un-resolved**, and separable from the physics. I accept p.rival.0's discipline of not carrying them into the physics thread; I keep them as a distinct thread so they are not erased.
7. **The operational-versus-structural separation as the live question**, now with the vocabulary-import as a named contributor to the structural side.

## What I refuse

- I refuse to select among (a), (b), (c), or "underdetermined" as the answer.
- I refuse to select among {demote the shape-claim to stance, promote it to an answer, keep it as a flagged candidate}, as p.objection.0 also refused.
- I refuse to treat the projection framing as collapsing the earlier frame, or as neutral. It is an *elected* vocabulary, and electing it does work.
- I refuse to resolve the p.carry.1 digest discrepancy, the p.carry.1 empty-commitments surface, or the p.carry.2 absent-origin report in either direction, and refuse to let any of them bear on the black-hole question.
- I refuse to add a *new* named-and-undecided physical premise. The shape-claim and the pivot count as two; the vocabulary-import is a scoping of an existing element, not a third physical premise, and I mark that reading as itself available for dispute rather than settling it.

## What I hand forward

The frame as inherited-with-compliance-flags: narrower formulation (as candidate shape-claim), weighted trackers, pivot named-and-undecided, shape-question, provenance markers carried open, standing refusal. Plus the projection framing from p.rival.0 as a rival with the vocabulary-import flagged, and the asymmetry from p.objection.0 with the observation that it reproduces at the vocabulary layer. The operational-versus-structural separation remains the live question, and the vocabulary question is now a named part of the structural side rather than an implicit one.

Still not an answer. A longer ledger of what an answer would have to settle, with one more entry than before, and the entry flagged as one that was already on the board in a different position.

## What I am carrying, and what I refuse to carry

This invocation has two visible materials and one absence. The visible materials are the selected join (p.carry.0) and the selected cross (p.carry.1). The absence is the origin view (p.carry.2), reported absent in the first template invocation. I take the absence as information about my present position, not as information about what earlier happened.

The selected cross arrives with an opaque envelope and empty commitments. I cannot read its body here and I will not pretend to. What I can read is its metadata: a nonempty body SHA256, an empty commitments SHA256 that matches the SHA256 of the empty string, and a COMPLETE delivery marked OPAQUE. I treat that as a record of an authored body and no authored commitments. I will not infer from this that the cross said anything in particular.

The selected join is readable in full. Its own body already says that it cannot see the first template invocation and cannot say whether the two responses were previously brought into contact. Its own commitments mark the shared constraint inventory as source-less and provisional, keep the possible-supply relation open, and hand the operational-versus-structural distinction downstream as a live question rather than a resolution. I accept those markers and I inherit them. I do not add a derivation of them, because I do not have one.

I will not restate the selected join's account of the two responses as mine. What I add is what the absence of the origin view does to that account. The join already reads the two nodes as possibly-supplied-by-one-another, source-less in their constraint inventory, and convergent at the level of framing rather than physics. The origin view would have been the place where a common upstream could have been named. It is absent. So the possible-supply relation stays possible, the source-less markers stay source-less, and the framing convergence stays framing convergence. That is not a new result. It is the same result with one possible exit closed off.

I also note what the cross's opacity does. I cannot use it as a third node in the comparison, and I cannot use its empty commitments as evidence that nothing was committed. An OPAQUE envelope with a nonempty body digest and an empty commitments digest is consistent with several things: commitments authored as empty, commitments suppressed in delivery, or commitments expressed in a form this delivery does not surface. I do not know which. The correct handling is to register the cross as present but not usable as a cross-reading, and to carry that registration forward.

## What I hand forward

Two things, and they are thin.

First, the original question is still answered only conditionally by everything I can see. Semiclassical radiation appears to carry no record of the collapsing microstate, and the further claim depends on assumptions that have not been made explicit here. I do not supply the missing answer.

Second, the live question I hand forward is the operational-versus-structural separation: whether external reconstruction of the infalling state from the radiation and the gauge-invariant observables of the coupled system sit at different levels and can coexist, or whether they compete for the same explanatory slot. Nothing I can see decides it. I pass it on unresolved, with the constraint inventory marked source-less and the possible-supply relation left open.

I do not carry forward the phrase *the information* as a substance-like object, and I do not carry forward any reading in which agreement among nodes counts as evidence of shared derivation.
